reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports the general utility of active-learning MLIPs for multicomponent alloys and mentions automatic training-set generation, but it does not provide specific evidence that such potentials can capture electron-vibration coupling or anharmonic vibrational entropy, nor does it demonstrate the claimed order-of-magnitude cost reduction for fusion free-energy calculations. The key premises regarding entropy contributions and cost savings are therefore largely unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: MLIP trained via active learning on targeted AIMD data can capture anharmonicity, vibrational entropy, and electron-vibration coupling
Active learning automatically generates a training set tailored to a given class of systems and properties with minimal DFT calculations
MLIPs are not limited by supercell size, enabling proper configurational averaging in multicomponent alloys
The approach will reduce computational cost by roughly an order of magnitude compared to full AIMD or TOR-TILD
